facilities.notes: Facility URL https://juneauicefield.org/lemon-creek-glacier returns 404; suggest replacing with the USGS Lemon Creek Glacier page. USGS page: mass balance measurements began 1953 under the direction of JIRP; today it is a USGS Benchmark Glacier with USGS Alaska Science Center contacts (McNeil, Sass, Frederick) plus Florentine (NRMSC). Sass's USGS profile says he leads the Alaska portion of the Benchmark Glacier Project. The JIRP history page names Maynard Miller (with William Field) as JIRP's founder, but no fetched page names a founding PI for Lemon Creek itself, so no founding-PI row was added. Current JIRP staff (Director of Operations Annie Boucher Krumdieck, Program Manager Tahi Wiggins) are not tied to Lemon Creek on any fetched page and were not added. Mauri Pelto co-authored the USGS Taku/Lemon Creek reanalysis, but no fetched page gives him a current Lemon Creek role.

The USGS South Cascade page lists Caitlyn Florentine (USGS Northern Rocky Mountain Science Center) as its only contact. The Portland State glacier-group history page (glaciers.us mirror of glaciers.research.pdx.edu) says Mark F. Meier started the USGS study (work began in 1957) and supervised it for 30 years. It also says Andrew Fountain joined the project in the late 1970s, so he is not the founding PI: his existing founding-PI row is corrected to a past scientist role. USGS OFR 98-031 confirms that Meier led the USGS Tacoma glaciology group, which ran mass-balance work on South Cascade, and that he retired from USGS in 1985.

people.name: Louis Sass, III
people.bio: Physical scientist with the USGS Alaska Science Center since 2012, leading the Alaska component of the USGS Benchmark Glacier Project, which tracks seasonal mass change on five U.S. glaciers. He focuses on accurate measurement of glacier change, the physical drivers and feedbacks behind it, and how glaciers shape streamflow. M.S., Alaska Pacific University.
people.research_interests: glacier mass balance; physical processes and feedbacks of glacier mass balance; glacier influences on streamflow

people.name: Christopher McNeil
people.bio: Geophysicist at the USGS Alaska Science Center in Anchorage. Studies how glacier extent, volume and mass change across basins and mountain ranges, and what those changes mean for ecosystems and sea level. His work includes reanalysis of the long USGS benchmark glacier records, combining field data with aerial and satellite imagery.
people.research_interests: glaciology; geodesy; climatology; remote sensing of glacier change; glacier mass balance reanalysis

people.name: Caitlyn Florentine
people.bio: Research physical scientist at the USGS Northern Rocky Mountain Science Center in Bozeman, Montana. A quantitative glaciologist, she studies glacier flow physics and glacier–climate links using field data, remote sensing and simple numerical models, and works with the USGS Glaciers and Climate Project. Ph.D. in geosciences, University of Montana (2018).
people.research_interests: quantitative glaciology; glacier flow physics; glacier-climate relationships; avalanche science; alpine and Arctic geomorphology, ecology and hydrology

people.name: Mark F. Meier
people.bio: USGS glaciologist hired in the mid-1950s who built the Water Resources Division's glaciology group in Tacoma, Washington. Under his leadership the group began long-term glacier monitoring, including mass-balance measurements on South Cascade Glacier. He retired from the USGS in 1985.

people.name: Andrew G. Fountain
people.bio: Professor Emeritus of Geology at Portland State University. His career has centred on the study of ice, chiefly glaciers, and he remains active in ice research in retirement.

people.name: Daniel Fisher
people.bio: Snow Survey Program Manager on the USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service Snow, Water and Climate staff in Palmer, Alaska. The group issues the Alaska Water Supply Outlook Reports, which combine manual snow courses and automated SNOTEL stations; the report also lists him as a hydrologist at the NRCS Snow Survey Office.
